newsitem.title: FRANCE: Britain's Blair says he'll meet France's Jospin.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Blair says he'll meet France's Jospin.

text.p: British Prime Minister Tony Blair said on Monday that he would meet his French Socialist counterpart Lionel Jospin during a weeklong holiday stay in southwestern France.
"I know he lives nearby. We will see one another," Blair, flanked by his wife and children, told reporters during a stroll through the village of Saint Martin d'Oydes.
He said he and Jospin would probably discuss current events, European matters and ties between Paris and London.
Blair did not say when the meeting would take place but officials in London said earlier on Monday that it would be on Friday at "a private lunch chez the prime minister (Blair)".

The British leader, his wife Cherie and their children, Nicolas, Kathryn and Euan, arrived in France from Italy on Saturday for the second leg of a summer holiday. They began their break in Tuscany, where Blair met Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi in Bologna on August 2.
They were expected to remain in the French village for about a week, staying at the home of David Keene, a London lawyer.
Saint Martin d'Oydes is 30 km (20 miles) from Jospin's constituency of Cintegabelle.

Speaking mostly in French, Blair told a throng of French and British journalists on Monday that he enjoyed the area and planned to spend time at the swimming pool, visit local tourist sites and see friends.
Trailed by the media, he then walked in sweltering heat to the village grocery shop where he bought ice cream bars for his children. REUTER
